title: Builder Signals · 2026-08-06
summary: Follow Builders 今日捕捉到 35 条 X 动态、1 集播客、0 篇博客；本站精选 10 条高信号内容。

featured.title: Madhu Guru · Meta AI 高级总监（前 Google，主导 Gemini / Veo / Nano Banana）
featured.summaryEn: Madhu Guru posted a two-part "model selection playbook" that's becoming standard among founders: prototype with the best frontier model, cost be damned, and validate the user experience first. Then 6–8 weeks later, when open-weight models catch up, move production workloads to them (and to smaller models where possible)—in that order. Don't start with the cheapest model. He notes most teams get stuck in step one, optimizing for cost and latency before they've validated what users actually want. The best model for…
featured.insightZh: Madhu Guru 这几天连发两条，给 builders 提炼了一套正在形成共识的「模型选型剧本」：先用最强前沿模型做原型，成本先放一边，把用户体验和真正的需求验证清楚；等 6–8 周后开源权重模型追上来、或者小模型能胜任时，再把生产负载迁过去。顺序不能反——不要一上来就抠最便宜的模型。他观察到大多数团队恰恰卡在第一步：还没验证清楚 UX 就急着优化成本和延迟。核心一句：早期产品验证的最佳模型，几乎从来不是上生产的最佳模型。

featured.title: Aaron Levie · Box CEO
featured.summaryEn: Drawing on constant enterprise contact, Aaron Levie made a call that's especially useful for consultancies and integrators: the diversity of AI implementation strategies far exceeds cloud's early days. Cloud had only a couple of deployment patterns and infra vendors; AI has a much wider range in the enterprise. Ask 10 IT leaders about their coding-agent strategy and you get at least 5 different answers. Some standardize end-user agents on ChatGPT/Claude, others offer multiple options, many build their own orchestr…
featured.insightZh: Aaron Levie 从跟大量企业打交道的一线视角，给出了一个对咨询与集成商很有价值的判断：企业 AI 落地的「打法多样性」远超当年云计算早期。云早期基本只有几种部署模式、几家基础设施厂商可选；而 AI 时代企业的策略五花八门——问 10 个 IT leader 他们的编程 agent 策略，能得到至少 5 种不同答案。终端生产力 agent 有的标准化到 ChatGPT/Claude，有的给员工多方案选择，还有的自建编排层接任意模型。模型层面，越来越多企业在试开源模型，或对「安全的开源方案」跃跃欲试；垂直模型和垂直 agent 也在涌现。数据访问上，有的让 agent 直接扮演用户角色，有的给 agent 设独立身份。他的结论：这么早期就如此异构，意味着未来数年格局还会剧烈变化，任何现在断言「最终赢家」的人大概率会错——机会还很多。

featured.title: Chai Discovery 的「苦涩教训」：药物设计也是一个 Scaling 问题
featured.summaryEn: Treating biology as another scaling problem—training molecule-design models the way you'd train an LLM by scaling compute, data and models—is turning drug "discovery" (needle-in-a-haystack screening) into drug "design" (generating the molecule you want directly on the computer), and the most counterintuitive lesson is that simplicity beats stacking modules. Chai Discovery co-founders Josh and Matt (Matt was on the early OpenAI team through GPT-1/2 and scaling laws) explain how they brought The Bitter Lesson into biology. The core idea: traditional discovery screens millions to billions of molecules to find one that works; Chai wants "design"—you feed in the dream molecule as a prompt and the model materializes it. Antibody design was long thought too hard (not enough data in the protein databank), yet that "holy grail" is exactly what they cracked. The most counterintuitive lesson is si…
featured.insightZh: 把生物学当成又一个 scaling 问题来做——像堆算力、堆数据训练 LLM 一样训练分子设计模型——正在把药物「发现」（大海捞针式筛选）变成药物「设计」（在电脑上直接生成你要的分子），而这背后最反直觉的一课是「简单性」压倒「模块堆砌」。 Chai Discovery 两位联创 Josh 和 Matt（Matt 曾在早期 OpenAI 参与 GPT-1/2 和 scaling laws 工作）在这期节目里，讲清了他们如何把「苦涩教训」（The Bitter Lesson）搬进生物学。核心思路：传统药物发现是「大海捞针」，筛选数百万上亿个分子找出一个能用的；而 Chai 想做的是「药物设计」——你把「理想分子的样子」作为 prompt 输进模型，模型直接把它物化出来。抗体设计一直被认为太难（蛋白质数据库里数据不够），但正是这个「圣杯」被他们攻下了。 最反直觉的一课是简单性。他们发现前代模型 CHI-1 有 23 个独立子模块，迭代时必须逐个理解每个模块的行为与动态，根本 scale 不动。于是他们坚持一个原则：不轻易加第 24 个模块——每次都逼问自己「这是增量补丁，还是可复利的根本改进？会不会帮我们泛化到一整类目标？」他们相信只要 scaling laws 成立、把 loss 继续压下去，模型就必须学会目标蛋白那些隐藏特征（比如糖基化位点），那些「难 target」就会随更强的模型自动解锁，而不是靠临时打补丁。 成果验证了这条路：抗体设计的结合成功率，从行业最先进的 0.1%（千里挑一），被 CHI-2 拉到了约 15%（千里挑 150）——这个量级让他们第一次能对分子的药物性质做有意义的统计并 hill climb。他们强调生物其实是可验证域：虽然湿实验读数要几天到几周、误差棒也大，但你能对「能不能结合、能不能量产」等属性给出客观读数，逼你对「是否真的在进步」保持诚实。团队刻意保持小而过载，倒逼优先级；联创 Jack 的名言是「想长期跑得快，短期有时得慢一点」——绝不为赶下一个结果牺牲可复利的代码质量。他们判断几个月前刚跨过采纳的临界点（所以最近大药厂纷纷官宣合作）…

items.title: Zara Zhang · Builder / Follow Builders 作者
items.summaryEn: Zara's three posts this week all circle the sociology of AI adoption—pointed reading for anyone running enterprise AI enablement. First, via a book: most people won't adopt a technology just because it makes them more efficient—adoption is an emotional, not rational, decision. People adopt because someone similar to them adopted it and got cooler/richer/more respected, or because they feel everyone around them has and they'll be left behind. So the messaging shouldn't be "this makes you 10x more efficient" but "so…
items.insightZh: Zara 这周三条都围绕「AI 采纳的社会学」，对做企业 AI enablement 的人尤其扎心。第一条借一本书讲清一个反直觉的事实：大多数人不会仅因为一项技术让自己更高效就采纳它——采纳是情感决策而非理性决策。人们采纳新技术，是因为「跟自己相似的某个人用了并变得更酷/更有钱/更受尊敬」，或因为「感觉身边人都用了、再不用就要掉队」。所以推动采纳的话术不该是「这能让你效率提升 10 倍」，而该是「跟你差不多的某某用了，生活变好了，你不想也这样吗」。技术扩散本质是一个社会过程。第二条落到具体做法：最好的 AI 培训不是课程，而是把一个 agent 拉进团队群里让大家围观它干活——每个搞「AI 赋能项目」的公司都该先试这招。第三条提出高效会议的判据：好会议不留待办清单，因为所有 action 都在会议中完成（由实时听会的 agent 或人当场做掉），「说」与「做」的间隔应为零，会议本身变成真正出活的工作时段。

items.title: Peter Yang · AI 教程创作者
items.summaryEn: Peter Yang dug into the business reality of vibe coding. His take: if you vibe code a SaaS today, it works better as a self-serve funnel into a more expensive services offering than as a way to make a lot of money on the SaaS itself—but the catch with services is it feels like consulting, selling "time for money" again. He half-joked that it's now easier to make money from X creator payouts than from a micro SaaS. He's also probing model economics: hearing GPT 5.6 Luna High is much cheaper with basically unlimited…
items.insightZh: Peter Yang 这周聊了 vibe coding 的商业化现实。他的观点：现在如果你 vibe code 出一个 SaaS，它更适合当作一个「自助漏斗」，把用户导向一个更贵的服务型产品，而不是指望靠 SaaS 本身赚大钱——但服务型生意的问题在于，它又回到了「拿时间换钱」的咨询老路。他甚至半开玩笑说，如今从 X 平台的创作者分成里赚钱，比从一个 micro SaaS 里赚钱还容易。另外他也在体验模型经济学：听说 GPT 5.6 Luna High 便宜很多、基本无限量，正好他的 Sol 额度快用完了——但他关心的是它能不能扛复杂的浏览器自动化任务，那占了他 Codex 使用量的一半。

items.title: Guillermo Rauch · Vercel CEO
items.summaryEn: Guillermo Rauch's posts this week were pure engineer, revealing Vercel's progress on backends and cost optimization. One notes Vercel powers Factory AI's API services with Fluid compute, handling billions of requests per month. The other is more actionable: one line of code in the AI SDK saves 90%+ on DeepSeek v4 Flash AI Gateway tokens. For teams running production LLM workloads and watching the bill, these "one line, 90% off" routing/caching optimizations are worth a look.
items.insightZh: Guillermo Rauch 这周的推文很「工程师」，透露了 Vercel 在后端和成本优化上的进展。一条讲 Vercel 用 Fluid compute 支撑 Factory AI 的 API 服务，每月处理数十亿次请求；另一条更实用：在 AI SDK 里加一行代码，就能在 DeepSeek v4 Flash 的 AI Gateway 上省下 90% 甚至更多的 token 成本。对正在跑生产 LLM 负载、盯着账单的团队，这类「一行省九成」的路由/缓存优化值得关注。

items.title: Aditya Agarwal · SPC 普通合伙人（前 Dropbox CTO）
items.summaryEn: Aditya Agarwal shared an interesting pattern and a technical view from the investor seat. The deal: Rivo—"self-driving finance." Agents connect to the checking account you already have, learn your cash flow, sweep dollars into Treasury-backed yield, and bring them back before bills hit—every dollar earning until the moment you spend it. Why it's hard: prediction under asymmetric cost—money returned a day early costs a little yield; a day late bounces a bill and destroys trust. He likens it to self-driving cars, wh…
items.insightZh: Aditya Agarwal 这周从投资视角讲了一个有意思的模式和一个技术观点。投资案例是 Rivo——「自动驾驶的钱」：agent 连接你已有的支票账户，学习你的现金流，把闲钱扫进国债支持的高收益产品，在账单到期前再取回来，让每一块钱在你花掉它之前都在生息。他点出这为什么难：在不对称成本下做预测——钱早还一天只损失一点收益，晚还一天却会跳票、摧毁信任。他把这类比自动驾驶汽车「最后那些 edge case 才是最难的」，只不过「自动驾驶的钱」失败模式更友好。另一条则强调：大规模部署 AI 的正确方式，是能够理解它是怎么工作的——LLM 不必是黑盒，可解释性是帮我们理解模型内部的关键一步。

items.title: Josh Woodward · Google Labs / Gemini App / AI Studio 副总裁
items.summaryEn: Josh Woodward shared a product-philosophy update for Google's Notebook (NotebookLM): "Notebook is built for thinking, not toggling." While others add more modes, Notebook keeps everything in a single, unified prompt bar and just does what you want—no switching back and forth. Ultra and Pro subscribers can jump in now, rolling out to everyone next. A clean example of "less is more, reduce cognitive load" product design.
items.insightZh: Josh Woodward 发布了 Google Notebook（NotebookLM）的产品理念更新：「Notebook 是为思考而造的，不是为切换模式而造的。」 当别家在不断堆加更多模式时，Notebook 反其道而行，把所有功能收进一个统一的 prompt bar，直接做你想做的事，不用来回切。Ultra 和 Pro 订阅用户已可体验，随后向所有人推送。这是产品设计上「少即是多、降低认知负担」的一个典型样本。

items.title: Swyx · Latent Space / smol.ai
items.summaryEn: Swyx had a "smol aha moment" at a Midjourney meetup that explains why knowledge graphs and ontologies are suddenly trending now rather than three years ago: because "good enough" intelligence is finally too cheap to meter. His logic: the hardest part of building KGs (using intelligence to extract and organize unstructured information into a graph) is now cheap; when intelligence gets commoditized, its complements—structured knowledge, graphs—rise in value. That's why talks on KGs from people like Frank Coyle and E…
items.insightZh: Swyx 在一场 Midjourney meetup 上有个「smol aha moment」，点破了知识图谱（KG）和本体论（ontology）为什么现在突然火起来、而不是三年前：因为「够用的」智能终于便宜到不值一提了。他的逻辑是——构建知识图谱最难的那部分（用智能把非结构化信息抽取、组织成图），现在成本极低；当智能被商品化，它的「互补品」（结构化知识、图谱）价值就会上升。这也是为什么 Frank Coyle、Emil Eifrem 这类讲知识图谱的 talk 最近特别受关注。

items.title: Sam Altman · OpenAI CEO
items.summaryEn: Sam Altman posted a values manifesto: he'd rather be an optimist who works hard than a pessimist posting about why things won't work. He acknowledges it's more difficult and the most likely path is failure—but society fails if people don't try, and no amount of "it will never work" essays will drive society forward.
items.insightZh: Sam Altman 发了条价值观宣言：他宁愿做一个努力干活的乐观主义者，也不做一个发帖论证「为什么这事儿成不了」的悲观主义者。他承认乐观这条路更难走、最可能的结局是失败，但如果人们不去尝试，社会就会失败——再多「它永远成不了」的檄文也无法推动社会前进。
